prs.title: feat(oxfmt): support Astro via `prettier-plugin-astro@1.x`
prs.author: leaysgur
prs.body:
Closes #19715

---

Support `.astro` files and also embedded `astro` via `prettier-plugin-astro@1.x`.

Prerequisites are the same as Svelte support.

- You need `@astrojs/compiler-rs` installed and executable through the Node.js process
  - (it should be there in existing Astro project anyway)
- Opt-in `astro: true` or `astro: { ... }` in your config

Notable differences:

- Frontmatter and `<script>` block are formatted by `oxc_formatter`
  - `<style>` block is still formatted by Prettier which may differ from `oxc_formatter_css`, same with other languages
- `<style lang="sass">` block is NOT formatted, while original plugin formats
  - May revisit in the future, but not for now
- `allowShortHand` is default unset, while accepts only `true|false`
  - No way to reset in `overrides`, same with Prettier

prs.title: fix(semantic): mark delete of optional members as MemberWriteTarget
prs.author: Bartok9
prs.body:
Fixes #27419

`delete a.b` marks `a` as `Read | MemberWriteTarget`. `delete a?.b` and `delete (a.b)` did not, because `visit_unary_expression` only set the write context when `argument.is_member_expression()`. An optional chain is a `ChainExpression`, and parentheses wrap the member, so the check failed and `visit_member_expression` never saw a write.

Unwrap parentheses/type assertions, and treat a chain whose element is a member (not a call) as a delete target. Bare `delete x` is unchanged.

Rolldown reads `MemberWriteTarget` to detect writes through member chains (rolldown/rolldown#11146).

refactor(oxfmt): unify language name tables into `Language` enum
prs.author: leaysgur
prs.body:
Before:

```
fence / embedded name --> dispatcher::route()      (its own match + JS ext fallback) --> Route
LSP languageId -------> get_file_extension_from_language_id  (its own match)  --> fake path ext
```

After:

```
embedded name --from_embedded--+
                               +--> Language --route()-----------> Route (Native | Prettier)
LSP languageId --from_lsp_id---+       |
                                       +--to_lsp_extension()----> fake path ext (LSP in-memory)

route_embedded(name) = from_embedded(name) -> Language::route()
                       or, for `mjs` / `cjs` / `mts` / `cts`, SourceType with that module kind
```

prs.title: refactor(oxfmt): clarify `handlebars` and `glimmer` relationship
prs.author: leaysgur
prs.body:
- Prettier supports `.hbs` and `.handlebars` files
- But it is formatted by `glimmer` parser
- And Glimmer (= legacy Ember template) does not allow loose syntax like snippet which is valid Handlebars
- Plus, Glimmer (= modern Ember template using `.gjs` and `.gts`) is also not supported

So, at present, what is referred to as "Handlebars support" actually only supports the old Glimmer template files.

prs.title: fix(transformer): avoid synthetic private fields for static blocks
prs.author: KurodaKayn
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #27244.

Lowering each static block to a synthetic private static field can introduce a field after earlier static initialization has made the class non-extensible. Under the proposal to make non-extensibility apply to private fields, this adds an observable TypeError.

This change folds blocks into subsequent static field initializers and defers trailing blocks through a closure initialized safely inside the class. Any synthetic carrier field is initialized before the deferred blocks execute.

## Changes

- Preserve static initialization order and class-expression results, including recursive initialization.
- Keep class declarations in their temporal dead zone until initialization completes, while preserving the separate inner class binding and export behavior.
- Preserve inferred function and class names, including computed, private, and symbol keys. Capture computed names for each class evaluation so later evaluations cannot overwrite them.
- Fix the CommonJS and ESM `setFunctionName` helpers to distinguish `Symbol("")` from `Symbol()`, producing `"[]"` and `""` respectively.
- Introduce wrapper scopes only when the transformation needs temporary bindings.
- Add regression fixtures and update expected outputs and conformance reports.

prs.title: refactor(transformer): simplify static block state
prs.author: Dunqing
prs.body:
Static-block lowering tracked inferred names, wrapper state, and deferred initializers across four separate containers. Consolidate them into one pending map and one class-state stack. Class expressions retain their state until expression exit, removing the deferred-initializer handoff between class and expression exits.

Classify static blocks and the last runtime static field in the existing private-key scan. Classes without blocks return before the lowering passes, and classes with blocks reuse the recorded carrier index instead of finding it again.

Share repeated arrow-call construction in a local helper while keeping binding creation and scope decisions at the call sites. The lowering rules and fixture outputs from #27300 remain unchanged.

Validation:

- `just fmt`, `just lint -p oxc_transformer`, and `just test -p oxc_transformer` (39 tests).
- Full transform conformance with `--exec`: all four reports match the exact-base baseline byte-for-byte, including existing failures.
- Rebuilt `napi/transform`: all 53 tests pass; the script-mode parameter-default direct-eval regression also passes through the rebuilt binding.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex.

prs.title: fix(minifier): eliminate unused IIFE calls with constant arguments
prs.author: Dunqing
prs.body:
Unused calls such as `const f = x => x + 1; f(1);` currently survive as `(x => x + 1)(1)`. Track constant arguments for arrow IIFEs and strict regular-function IIFEs so the existing constant folder and side-effect analysis can remove the call. Parameter constants guide folding without replacing bare parameter reads, avoiding duplicated argument literals.

The optimization preserves argument evaluation and respects parameter writes, redeclarations, and direct eval. It conservatively skips defaults, destructuring, rest parameters, and spread arguments, and preserves the existing DCE-only IIFE behavior. Regular functions are excluded when their own name is referenced or when they are non-strict, since recursion and mapped arguments can invalidate the call's parameter values.

Regression coverage includes multiple parameters, nested closures, side effects, mixed BigInt arithmetic, argument duplication, recursion, and strict versus sloppy arguments aliasing.

Fixes #27379.

Validation:

- `just fmt`
- `just test -p oxc_minifier` — 723 tests and 2 doctests passed; 33 existing tests ignored
- `just lint -p oxc_minifier`
- `pnpm run build-test` and `pnpm test` in `napi/minify` — 890 tests passed; 14 skipped and 1 todo
- `just minsize` — size and allocation snapshots unchanged
- 586 runtime equivalence comparisons across 148 inputs through the Node API, with and without mangling, in module and script modes

prs.title: perf(linter): share one source per file across type-aware diagnostics
prs.author: maschwenk
prs.body:
`DiagnosticHandler::send_diagnostic` in `crates/oxc_linter/src/tsgolint.rs` copied the file's whole source text into every type-aware diagnostic it sent: `get_source_text(path).to_string()`, then `NamedSource::new(.., source_text.to_owned())` in `wrap_diagnostics`. Each copy lives as long as its diagnostic, so the oxlint process grows with diagnostics × file size.

This builds one `Arc<NamedSource>` per file (new `DiagnosticService::named_source`, which `wrap_diagnostics` now uses too) and shares it across that file's diagnostics. Output is unchanged.

vscode `src` (10,201 files) with every type-aware rule enabled, `oxlint --type-aware` with oxlint-tsgolint 7.0.2003, 316k diagnostics, release build on an 18-core Mac, two runs each:

| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| oxlint process, peak RSS | 30.5 / 31.8 GiB | 0.7 / 0.7 GiB |
| oxlint + tsgolint, peak RSS | 39.5 / 41.0 GiB | 10.0 / 10.0 GiB |
| wall | 24.0 / 18.8 s | 18.1 / 15.8 s |

The build measured here also carries the in-process tsrs backend from the draft below, which is inactive when oxlint runs the Go tsgolint. On a 27k-file project with 21 diagnostics, time and memory do not change.

Checked: the type-aware fixture tests (`cargo test -p oxlint -- tsgolint`, 27) pass unchanged, as do `oxc_diagnostics` and `oxc_linter`'s unit tests; clippy is clean with warnings denied.

Also the second commit of:

- https://github.com/oxc-project/oxc/pull/27461

prs.title: perf(packages/codegen): reduce writes for optional `MemberExpression`s
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Small perf optimization.

When printing optional member expression `?.`, print `?.` in a single write, instead of writing `?` and `.` individually. 1 less `write` call for this case, and it also shortens the path to a single `write` call for all cases.

prs.title: perf(packages/codegen): reduce writes and branches printing functions
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Perf optimization.

When printing a `function`, `node.async` is fairly unpredictable - some functions are async, others aren't.

Make whether to print the `async` keyword a branchless decision.

Also use a single write in all cases to print the whole prefix of the function (e.g. `function`, `declare async function` etc). The main win here is to avoid printing a single space as a separate `write` call in the common case of named functions.

prs.title: docs(packages/codegen): correct doc comment for `printBinaryish`
refactor(packages/codegen): import ESTree types individually
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Pure refactor.

Import ESTree types individually to shorten the code where these types are used.

prs.title: perf(packages/codegen): reduce megamorphic property accesses in `printBinaryish`
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Perf optimization.

Accessing the a `type` property of an `Expression` is expensive because an `Expression` can be any one of many object shapes, so it's a slow megamorphic access. In `printBinaryish` (a hot path), ensure that each of these accesses happens only once, rather than multiple times.

This change shows a 1%-2% perf improvement on most bench fixtures.

prs.title: perf(packages/codegen): reduce megamorphic property accesses for `BinaryExpression`s
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Perf optimization. Continuation of #27458.

The branch of `printExpression` for `BinaryExpression` (common path) reads the `type` of the left-hand node in order to check if it's a `PrivateInExpression`. This is a costly megamorphic access.

In the common case where it's _not_ a `PrivateInExpression`, it then calls `printBinaryish` which then accesses `node.left.type` again. This incurs the megamorphic load cost twice.

Instead, pass the extracted value of `node.left.type` into `printBinaryish` so it can avoid the 2nd lookup.

prs.title: perf(packages/codegen): reduce megamorphic `type` reads in `binCheckAndPrepare`
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Perf optimization. Continuation of #27458.

Ensure that costly megamorphic reads of the `type` of `Expression`s happens the minimum of times.

Pass `left` (with any `ParenthesizedExpression` wrappers stripped off) and `left.type` into `binCheckAndPrepare`, so in the paths for `??` and `**`, the unwrapping and megamorphic `.type` accesses don't need to be repeated again. `**` is rare, but `??` is quite heavily used in some codebases.

Passing these 2 vars as params doesn't cost anything, as `binCheckAndPrepare` gets inlined anyway.

prs.title: feat(oxfmt/lsp): show root config errors to LSP client
prs.author: Sysix
prs.body:
## Summary
This PR improves the oxfmt LSP server's error reporting by propagating root configuration resolution errors to the language server client as notification messages. Previously, configuration errors were only logged via `warn!` macros, making them invisible to users in their editors.

## Problem
When the oxfmt LSP server encountered configuration errors (e.g., invalid `.oxfmtrc.json`, missing required files), these errors were silently logged on the server side. Users had no visibility into why formatting wasn't working or configuration wasn't being applied, resulting in poor debugging experience.

## Solution
The PR modifies the configuration loading pipeline to:
1. Capture configuration errors as `ClientMessage` structs containing the error message and message type
2. Propagate these messages through the `ServerFormatterBuilder` and `ServerFormatter::new()` initialization flow
3. Return collected messages alongside the formatter instance
4. Display these messages to the client via LSP `ShowMessage` notifications during initialization and on config changes
